patch.objective: Creating and managing encryption keys and certificates across one or many Regions with KMS customer managed keys and AWS Private Certificate Authority

sources.cite: AWS Certified Security - Specialty (SCS-C03) exam guide: Detection 16%, Incident Response 14%, Infrastructure Security 18%, Identity and Access Management 20%, Data Protection 18%, Security Foundations and Governance 14%
sources.note: Overview and the Domain 4 page read directly (markdown) on 2026-11-17. Domain weights as above; Skill 4.2.3 'Design, interpret, and implement IAM policies by following the principle of least privilege (for example, permission boundaries, session policies)'; 4.2.5 'Investigate and correct unintended permissions'. Domains 1, 3 and 5 wording is the course seed's; those pages were not re-read. (read for this round by an earlier pass on 2026-11-17)

sources.cite: AWS KMS Developer Guide, Allowing users in other accounts to use a KMS key
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-17. Quoted: 'Neither the key policy nor the IAM policy alone is sufficient - you must change both'; the key policy in the owning account must give the external account (or its roles) permission; IAM policies in the external account delegate it, and can only grant actions the key policy also allows. The KMS guide (read 2026-11-18): 'AWS KMS retains all key material for a KMS key ... AWS KMS deletes key material only when you delete the KMS key', and decryption automatically uses the version that encrypted the data (rotate-keys.html); 'You cannot change the key policies of AWS managed keys' (key-policy-modifying.html).
